title: Clarify terminal vs transient error semantics across SDKs
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Background:
Redwood SDKs currently surface a variety of error shapes across Python/TypeScript/Go. Engineers have inconsistent guidance about which failures are terminal (do not retry) versus transient (safe to retry with backoff), how streaming interruptions should be surfaced (resumable vs terminal), and what contextual hints (retry-after, idempotency tokens, resume cursors) are provided. This ambiguity leads to app-level incorrect retries or over-retries, poor UX for streaming clients, and noisy support tickets.

Goal:
Define a clear, language-agnostic error semantics spec and specific SDK error classes/types for Python, TypeScript, and Go. Provide actionable messages and structured hint fields that client apps can consume to make safe retry/resume decisions. Produce examples and tests that SDKs can adopt.

Non-goals:
- Final wire format of server telemetry (server team will publish model-level error codes separately).
- Full SDK refactor — scope to adapter layer and public API contracts only.

Proposal summary:
1) Error categories: Terminal, Transient, RateLimit, Auth (fatal until refreshed), Cancelled (client-initiated), StreamingResumeable. Each category maps to a canonical error code string (e.g., ERR_TERMINAL, ERR_TRANSIENT, ERR_RATE_LIMIT, ERR_AUTH, ERR_CANCELLED, ERR_STREAM_RESUMEABLE).
2) Error surface: Every SDK error object will include: code (canonical string), message (human text), retriable (true|false string for cross-language parity), retry_hint (optional string; e.g., "exponential", "linear"), retry_after (optional RFC3339 timestamp or seconds), resume_cursor (optional string for streaming resume), idempotency_key_required (optional "true"/"false"). NOTE: values are surfaced programmatically (typed in each SDK) and message remains readable for developers.
3) Python/TS/Go bindings:
   - Python: new exception base class RedwoodSDKError with attrs: code:str, retriable:bool, retry_after:Optional[datetime], resume_cursor:Optional[str], idempotency_required:bool. Provide helpers is_retriable(err) and extract_resume(err).
   - TypeScript: exported type RedwoodError extends Error with properties code:string, retriable:boolean, retryAfter?:number, resumeCursor?:string, idempotencyRequired?:boolean. Add isRetriable(err) util.
   - Go: error values implement interface RedwoodError { Code() string; Retriable() bool; RetryAfter() time.Time; ResumeCursor() string; IdempotencyRequired() bool }. Provide helper functions errors.IsRetriable(err) and errors.ResumeCursor(err).
4) Streaming behavior: Streaming interruptions where a resume_cursor is provided will be surfaced as StreamingResumeable with retriable=true and resume_cursor filled. If no resume_cursor, surface as Terminal (retriable=false). SDK streaming clients should expose a resume() helper that accepts cursor/token.
5) Retry guidance: Server will prefer to communicate retry-after in seconds for RateLimit and Transient. SDKs implement default: exponential backoff with jitter capped at 30s for transient, linear backoff for rate_limit respecting retry_after when present. Provide explicit docs and examples for idempotent vs non-idempotent operations.
6) Upgrade path: Implement adapter layer that normalizes server error payloads into canonical SDK errors. Keep backward compatibility by preserving original message in .raw or .details field for 6 months before deprecating.

Acceptance criteria:
- Spec document committed to sdk/ERRORS.md explaining codes, fields, and language bindings.
- Python/TS/Go adapters implemented that map server errors to new types (unit tests with >90% coverage across mapping cases).
- Example snippets for retries and streaming resume added to SDK README pages.
- E2E smoke test where a simulated transient error + retry succeeds and a simulated streaming interruption with resume_cursor correctly resumes.
- SDK packages publish minor releases containing the new error types and helper functions.

Implementation plan (high level):
- Week 1: Finalize canonical codes and fields, write ERRORS.md and cross-language API sketches.
- Week 2: Implement adapter mapping and public types in Python/TS. Add unit tests and example notebooks.
- Week 3: Implement Go interface and helpers, run cross-language integration tests (streaming simulator).
- Week 4: Docs, publish releases, and soft-deprecate old fields with migration notes.

Notes on backward compatibility and migration:
- For each SDK, the adapter will add new typed fields but preserve old error string/generic error for at least one release. Migration guide will include search/replace examples and error-handling patterns.
- Telemetry: SDKs will emit an attribute error.code for all surfaced errors to help server and product teams track distribution of codes.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: Server payloads may be inconsistent. Mitigation: adapter includes a robust parser and a default fallback mapping rule that marks unknown errors as ERR_TRANSIENT and sets retriable=false until server-side mapping improves.
- Risk: Developers rely on message text. Mitigation: emphasize code-based checks in docs and provide FAQ with examples.

Open questions:
- Should we standardize the exact retry policy parameters (base/backoff cap) across SDKs or make them configurable by default? (proposal: provide a shared default but expose config).
- How long do we preserve deprecated fields? (proposal: two releases, with warnings in logs).

Rollout and monitoring:
- Add dashboard tile in Console showing error.code distribution and fraction of retriable failures by route.
- Track adoption by release tag and number of clients using isRetriable helpers in telemetry (opt-in for privacy).
